steps.label: What they are
steps.why: A disc is a JOIN between two cells, which is why it shows up as a dark line running across the fibre.
common_mistakes: Calling them striations. Striations are the light and dark bands of the fibre; an intercalated disc marks the end of a cell.
Saying they are found in skeletal muscle. They are found only in cardiac muscle.
steps.memory_tip: Intercalated means placed between: the disc is the wall between two heart muscle cells.
steps.margin_note: What they look like and what they actually are. Two lines.

steps.label: Why they matter
steps.why: Without a quick path from cell to cell the chambers could not contract together, so the gap junction is the reason the heart beats as a single unit.
common_mistakes: Writing only that they are dark lines. The gap junctions and the quick spread of the impulse carry this mark.
steps.memory_tip: A gap junction is an open door: the impulse crosses without stopping, so the heart contracts as one.
steps.margin_note: Name gap junctions and say what they do. That is the whole second mark.

lines.text: Gap junctions pass the impulse from cell to cell

lines: The impulse passes through them from one cell
to the next without delay, so the whole heart
muscle contracts together as one unit.
